title: Bits, bytes, and digital data
description: How computers represent information as bits and group them into bytes before anything can travel on a network.
objectives: Explain what a bit and a byte are
Relate binary values to everyday digital data

diagnostic.question: How many bits are in one byte?
diagnostic.explanation: A byte is a group of 8 bits, the usual unit for a single character of text or a small piece of stored data.

title: How computers send and receive data
description: A host needs a network interface, an address, and a way to turn bytes into signals that another host can read.
objectives: Name the role of a network interface
Describe sending data as a request and a response

diagnostic.question: When your laptop visits a website, what is the laptop acting as?
options: A router for the whole internet
A client requesting a service
A DNS root server
A certificate authority
diagnostic.correctAnswer: A client requesting a service
diagnostic.explanation: Your computer is a client: it sends a request and the remote server replies with the page or API data.

title: What a network does
description: A network exists so independent devices can share information and services without each one connecting to every other one directly.
objectives: State why we build networks
Distinguish a link from a path of several hops

diagnostic.question: What is the main job of a computer network?
options: Store files only on one disk
Let separate devices exchange data
Replace the need for IP addresses
Encrypt every cable by default
diagnostic.correctAnswer: Let separate devices exchange data
diagnostic.explanation: Networking is about moving data between independent devices so they can share services.

title: LANs, WANs, and the internet
description: Local networks cover a home or office; wide-area networks span cities; the internet is the public interconnection of many networks.
objectives: Contrast LAN, WAN, and the internet
Give an example of each

diagnostic.question: A home Wi-Fi network is best described as which of the following?
options: A WAN that spans countries
A LAN covering a small area
The public internet backbone
A DNS root zone
diagnostic.correctAnswer: A LAN covering a small area
diagnostic.explanation: A home or office network is a local area network (LAN). The internet is many such networks linked together.

title: Network devices and topologies
description: Switches, routers, and access points sit in star and mixed topologies so hosts do not have to cable directly to each other.
objectives: Identify switch, router, and access point roles
Recognize a star topology

diagnostic.question: Which device typically forwards Ethernet frames inside one LAN using MAC addresses?
options: A switch
A DNS resolver
A web browser
A certificate authority
diagnostic.correctAnswer: A switch
diagnostic.explanation: A switch learns MAC addresses and forwards frames on the local network. Routers forward IP packets between networks.

title: Why network protocols use layers
description: Layering lets each protocol handle one job—links, routing, reliable delivery, or applications—so they can be swapped independently.
objectives: Explain why protocols are layered
Map a familiar app onto application and transport layers

diagnostic.question: Why do networks use protocol layers instead of one giant protocol?
options: So each layer can change without rewriting every other job
Because cables can only carry one layer
So IP addresses become optional
Because browsers refuse unlayered packets
diagnostic.correctAnswer: So each layer can change without rewriting every other job
diagnostic.explanation: Layers isolate jobs: Ethernet can change without changing HTTP, and TCP can provide reliability without HTTP reimplementing it.

title: Encapsulation and packets
description: Each layer wraps the payload from the layer above with its own header, forming frames and packets that other devices can inspect.
objectives: Describe encapsulation
Name headers added for IP and Ethernet

diagnostic.question: When a web request leaves your laptop, which statement about encapsulation is true?
options: HTTP is wrapped by transport and IP headers, then a link-layer frame
The switch deletes the IP header on the LAN
Only the DNS header travels to the server
Encapsulation happens only on the server
diagnostic.correctAnswer: HTTP is wrapped by transport and IP headers, then a link-layer frame
diagnostic.explanation: Application data is encapsulated: HTTP inside TCP (or QUIC), inside IP, inside an Ethernet or Wi-Fi frame.

title: Ethernet and local networks
description: Ethernet is the common wired LAN technology: frames carry a destination MAC, a source MAC, and a payload for the next protocol.
objectives: Identify Ethernet frame addressing
Relate Ethernet to a local link

diagnostic.question: An Ethernet frame is delivered on a LAN using which kind of address?
options: A MAC address
A UDP port only
An autonomous system number
A TLS certificate fingerprint
diagnostic.correctAnswer: A MAC address
diagnostic.explanation: Ethernet uses 48-bit MAC addresses to deliver frames on the local link. IP addresses are used to route between networks.

title: MAC addresses and switching
description: Each interface has a MAC address. Switches learn which MAC sits on which port so they can forward frames instead of flooding forever.
objectives: Explain what a MAC address identifies
Describe how a switch learns ports

diagnostic.question: A switch forwards a frame to one port instead of every port because it has learned what?
options: Which MAC address was last seen on that port
The destination website's TLS certificate
The sender's username
The WAN default gateway's DNS name
diagnostic.correctAnswer: Which MAC address was last seen on that port
diagnostic.explanation: Switches build a MAC address table from source addresses so later frames to that MAC go only to the right port.

title: IPv4 and IPv6 addresses
description: IP addresses identify interfaces on an internetwork. IPv4 uses 32-bit dotted decimal; IPv6 uses 128-bit hexadecimal groups.
objectives: Read an IPv4 address and prefix
Recognize that IPv6 uses a larger address space

diagnostic.question: Which of these is a valid IPv4 address?
options: https://example.com
aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff
diagnostic.explanation: IPv4 addresses have four decimal numbers from 0 to 255. 300 is out of range; a MAC address uses hex pairs; a URL is not an IP address.

title: Subnet masks and subnetting
description: A subnet mask or prefix length splits an IP address into network and host parts so routers can group addresses into networks.
objectives: Split a simple address into network and host parts
Read slash notation such as /24

diagnostic.question: In 192.168.4.19/24, what does /24 tell you?
options: The first 24 bits are the network prefix
The host can use 24 IP addresses only
The LAN is limited to 24 switches
IPv6 must be used after 24 hops
diagnostic.correctAnswer: The first 24 bits are the network prefix
diagnostic.explanation: CIDR prefix length /24 means the first 24 bits identify the network; the remaining 8 bits identify hosts on that subnet.

title: Routers and IP routing
description: Routers forward packets between networks by matching the destination IP against routes, including a default route for everything else.
objectives: Contrast a router with a switch
Explain what a default gateway does

diagnostic.question: Your PC sends a packet to an address that is not on its own subnet. Where does it send that packet first?
options: To its configured default gateway
To a random MAC on the LAN
Straight to the distant web server's MAC
To UDP port 53 only
diagnostic.correctAnswer: To its configured default gateway
diagnostic.explanation: Hosts send off-subnet packets to the default gateway (a router), which then forwards based on IP routes.

title: ARP, Neighbor Discovery, and local delivery
description: IP still needs a local MAC. ARP (IPv4) and Neighbor Discovery (IPv6) map a next-hop IP address to a link-layer address on this LAN.
objectives: State why ARP or NDP is needed
Describe a next-hop lookup on a LAN

diagnostic.question: Why does a host use ARP on an IPv4 Ethernet LAN?
options: To learn the MAC address that matches a next-hop IPv4 address
To encrypt HTTP
To assign a public autonomous system number
To compress TCP headers
diagnostic.correctAnswer: To learn the MAC address that matches a next-hop IPv4 address
diagnostic.explanation: Ethernet delivers frames by MAC address. ARP answers “who has this IPv4 address?” so the frame can be addressed locally.

title: UDP and TCP
description: UDP sends datagrams with little setup. TCP adds ports, a handshake, retransmission, and ordered byte streams for applications that need reliability.
objectives: Contrast UDP and TCP
Explain what a port number identifies

diagnostic.question: Which statement about TCP versus UDP is accurate?
options: TCP provides retransmission and ordered delivery; UDP does not
UDP always handshakes before sending
TCP cannot use port numbers
UDP encrypts payloads by default
diagnostic.correctAnswer: TCP provides retransmission and ordered delivery; UDP does not
diagnostic.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented with acknowledgements and retransmission. UDP is a simple datagram service; encryption is a separate layer such as TLS or DTLS.

title: DNS and name resolution
description: DNS maps human names such as example.com to IP addresses by querying resolvers and, when needed, the hierarchical name servers.
objectives: Describe what a DNS query returns
Place DNS before a typical web request

diagnostic.question: What does DNS mainly do before your browser opens a website by name?
options: Translate the name into an IP address
Issue the site's TLS certificate
Assign your computer a MAC address
Compress the HTML
diagnostic.correctAnswer: Translate the name into an IP address
diagnostic.explanation: Packets are delivered to IP addresses. DNS resolves the name you typed into one or more addresses the client can connect to.

title: HTTP and HTTPS
description: HTTP is the application protocol for web requests and responses. HTTPS is HTTP over a TLS-protected connection, usually on port 443.
objectives: Read a simple HTTP request line
Explain how HTTPS differs from HTTP

diagnostic.question: HTTPS is best described as which of the following?
options: HTTP running inside a TLS-protected connection
A replacement for DNS
A switch protocol for MAC learning
Plain HTTP on port 80 with a longer timeout
diagnostic.correctAnswer: HTTP running inside a TLS-protected connection
diagnostic.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS. The HTTP methods and URLs are the same; the connection is encrypted and authenticated.

title: TLS and secure connections
description: TLS authenticates the server with certificates and encrypts the bytes so observers on the path cannot read or easily alter the application data.
objectives: State what a certificate is used for
Explain confidentiality versus authentication

diagnostic.question: What is the main purpose of a website's TLS certificate in HTTPS?
options: Help the client authenticate the server and set up encryption keys
Assign the site an IPv6 address
Replace the need for DNS
List the switch ports on the LAN
diagnostic.correctAnswer: Help the client authenticate the server and set up encryption keys
diagnostic.explanation: The certificate binds a public key to a name so the client can authenticate the server, then TLS derives keys that encrypt the session.

title: DHCP and getting online
description: DHCP automatic configuration gives a host an address, mask, default gateway, and usually DNS resolvers so it can join a network without static setup.
objectives: List the settings DHCP typically provides
Contrast DHCP with a static address

diagnostic.question: Which set of settings does DHCP commonly provide to a joining host?
options: IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS servers
Only a TLS private key
Only a MAC address burned into the NIC
An autonomous system number
diagnostic.correctAnswer: IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and DNS servers
diagnostic.explanation: A typical DHCP lease includes address, mask, gateway, and resolver information so the host can send packets off the LAN and look up names.

title: Wi-Fi and wireless networking
description: Wi-Fi is a wireless LAN. Stations associate with an access point that bridges wireless frames onto the wired Ethernet network.
objectives: Describe association with an access point
Relate Wi-Fi to Ethernet bridging

diagnostic.question: On a typical home network, what does the Wi-Fi access point do?
options: Lets wireless devices join the same LAN as wired Ethernet ports
Replaces the need for IP addresses
Runs the public DNS root
Issues TLS certificates for every laptop
diagnostic.correctAnswer: Lets wireless devices join the same LAN as wired Ethernet ports
diagnostic.explanation: The access point is a LAN bridge for wireless clients. Routing to the internet is a separate router function, often in the same box.

title: Firewalls and basic network security
description: A firewall allows or blocks packets using addresses and ports. Home routers often hide internal hosts with NAT as well as filtering.
objectives: Describe allow/deny using address and port
Recognize NAT as hiding internal addresses

diagnostic.question: A simple host firewall that blocks inbound TCP port 22 is making a decision based on what?
options: Addresses and transport ports in the packet headers
The colour of the Ethernet cable
The HTML of the website
The Wi-Fi channel number only
diagnostic.correctAnswer: Addresses and transport ports in the packet headers
diagnostic.explanation: Packet filters match IP addresses and TCP/UDP ports (and related state). They do not need the web page contents to block SSH on port 22.

title: A method for troubleshooting connectivity
description: Work from the host outward: address and gateway, then ping, then DNS, then the application. Ping and traceroute use ICMP to test a path.
objectives: Order basic connectivity checks
Interpret a failed DNS lookup versus a failed ping

diagnostic.question: A site name will not load, but pinging 8.8.8.8 works. Which check should you try next?
options: DNS resolution for the site name
Replacing the Ethernet switch immediately
Disabling IPv4 on every host
Deleting the default gateway
diagnostic.correctAnswer: DNS resolution for the site name
diagnostic.explanation: A working ping to a public IP shows IP routing is probably fine. Failure by name points to DNS or the application, not the whole path.

title: Trace a web request across a network
description: Follow one HTTPS request: DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP, and the return path through LAN, gateway, and the public internet.
objectives: Order DNS, TCP, TLS, and HTTP in a browser fetch
Name devices the packet may pass

diagnostic.question: Which order best describes a typical browser fetch of https://example.com?
options: DNS lookup, TCP handshake, TLS handshake, then HTTP request
HTTP request, then DNS, then ARP only
TLS certificate first, then DHCP, then UDP to port 80
Ping the MAC address, then skip DNS
diagnostic.correctAnswer: DNS lookup, TCP handshake, TLS handshake, then HTTP request
diagnostic.explanation: The client resolves the name, opens a TCP connection to the server address, performs TLS, then sends HTTP on that protected stream.
